schemes.official_name: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), offset mechanism
schemes.publisher: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Ministry of Power, Government of India
schemes.offers_text: BEE issues Carbon Credit Certificates to registered projects after verification under the offset procedure. One certificate represents one tonne of CO2e.
schemes.who: Entities not obligated under the compliance mechanism that register an eligible project in an approved offset sector and follow the published detailed procedure.
numbers_used: 1 Carbon Credit Certificate = 1 tCO2e (BEE carbon market page).

benefit.label: hypothetical gross certificate value, not issued credit or a sale
benefit.formula: issued certificates x your stated certificate price, before fees and without a confirmed buyer

schemes.publisher: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Ministry of Power, Government of India
schemes.offers_text: Obligated entities with emission intensity below their notified target may be issued Carbon Credit Certificates; entities above it surrender or buy certificates for the shortfall.

Nine sectors named for gradual transition (BEE carbon market page).

schemes.publisher: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India
schemes.offers_text: A subsidy on the official cost of Zero Defect Zero Effect (ZED) certification, plus other incentives listed on the scheme site.
schemes.who: Micro, small and medium enterprises with Udyam Registration; each unit applies for certification separately.
numbers_used: Subsidy on the cost of certification: micro 80%, small 60%, medium 50% (zed.msme.gov.in/subsidy-on-cost-of-certification).

Women-owned MSMEs: free ZED certification (notice "Free ZED Certification For Women Owned MSMEs" on zed.msme.gov.in, checked 16 Oct 2026). The subsidy page still lists women owners under the extra 10%; the later notice is followed here.
An additional 10% for SC/ST entrepreneurs or MSMEs in NER, Himalayan, LWE, island territories or aspirational districts; an additional 5% for SFURTI or MSE-CDP participants.
A one-time joining reward of Rs 10,000 after taking the ZED Pledge, deducted from the certification cost first.

benefit.reason: No current official ZED fee schedule is archived here (the scheme guidelines PDF was not read), and the subsidy applies only to that official fee, so no amount is calculated.

schemes.publisher: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
schemes.offers_text: Green project financing may be available. SIDBI's Green Finance Scheme page states term loans up to Rs 50 crore, at most 75% of project cost, repayment up to 10 years with up to 18 months moratorium, at an MCLR-linked rate.
schemes.who: Manufacturers, service providers and MSMEs on the supply or demand side of the green value chain, for activities such as energy efficiency, renewable energy, e-mobility and waste management.
numbers_used: Financing up to Rs 50 crore, subject to at most 75% of total project cost (sidbi.in/en/green-finance, re-read 16 Oct 2026).
Repayment up to 10 years with moratorium up to 18 months; MCLR-linked interest.
No rate concession is published.

benefit.label: first-year simple interest difference, not an offer
benefit.formula: loan amount x (your current rate - the rate you were offered), first year, simple interest

inputs.name: offered_rate_percent
inputs.label: Rate in an offer you actually received

schemes.official_name: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), definitive regime
schemes.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union
schemes.offers_text: Possible compliance exposure: from 1 January 2026 EU importers buy and surrender CBAM certificates for the embedded emissions of covered goods.
schemes.who: Exporters of cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity or hydrogen to the EU, through their EU importer. Check the CN code of the exact product.
numbers_used: CBAM certificate prices by import quarter: Q1 2026 EUR 75.36 (published 7 April 2026), Q2 2026 EUR 75.28 (6 July 2026), Q3 2026 EUR 82.32 (5 October 2026); Q4 2026 not yet published.
Certificate numbers also depend on the free-allocation adjustment and any carbon price already paid, which are not modelled here.

benefit.label: gross sensitivity for imports in {quarter}, before the free-allocation adjustment, carbon price already paid and importer obligations; not a buyer saving
benefit.formula: embedded tonnes x the published CBAM certificate price for that import quarter

schemes.official_name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) in Ireland
schemes.offers_text: Possible compliance exposure: a cap-and-trade scheme where installations surrender emission allowances and can trade them.
schemes.who: Operators of covered installations such as power stations and larger industrial plants (for example cement, lime and chemicals), as listed by the EPA.
numbers_used: The EPA page says the EU ETS limits emissions from more than 11,000 installations.

benefit.reason: Allowance needs depend on whether a site is a covered installation and its verified emissions; no amount is calculated.

schemes.official_name: Carbon Tax (Carbon Tax Act), administered by SARS
schemes.offers_text: Possible compliance exposure: a carbon tax with annual accounts and payments filed with SARS.
schemes.who: Entities liable under the Carbon Tax Act, as set out by SARS; check the Act and SARS guidance for thresholds.
numbers_used: SARS lists annual carbon tax accounts and payments filed on eFiling (EXD 180).

benefit.reason: Liability depends on facility activities, thresholds and allowances in the Act; no amount is calculated.

schemes.offers_text: Green project financing may be available: the taxonomy is the Central Bank of Kenya's classification banks use for green finance. It is guidance, not a loan or subsidy.
schemes.who: Projects and activities that banks classify as green under the taxonomy; check with a lender.
numbers_used: Published as the Kenya Green Finance Taxonomy, April 2025.

benefit.reason: The taxonomy classifies activities; it states no rate, amount or subsidy.

schemes.official_name: Exemption from the CO2 levy subject to a reduction obligation
schemes.publisher: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN), Switzerland
schemes.offers_text: Possible compliance exposure: the CO2 levy applies to heating fuels; operators of installations outside the ETS can apply for exemption by committing to a reduction obligation based on a target agreement with the federal government.
schemes.who: Operators of installations that are not in the Swiss ETS and carry out an economic activity or certain public-law activities, as described by the FOEN; check the CO2 Ordinance for conditions.
numbers_used: The FOEN business page states a CO2 levy of CHF 120 per tonne of CO2 from heating fuels.
A reduction obligation lasts until 2040, with an annual monitoring report and a decarbonisation plan updated every three years.

benefit.reason: The exemption value depends on fuel use, the target agreement and the levy redistribution rules; no amount is calculated.

schemes.official_name: Swiss Emissions Trading System (ETS) for installation operators
schemes.publisher: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN), Switzerland
schemes.offers_text: Possible compliance exposure: high-emitting installations must take part in the Swiss ETS, which has been linked with the EU ETS since 1 January 2020.
schemes.who: Installation operators carrying out an activity in Annex 6 of the CO2 Ordinance (the FOEN lists cement, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, refineries, paper, district heating and steel).
numbers_used: Sites whose emissions consistently fall below 25,000 tonnes CO2e a year may apply to opt out.
Voluntary participation needs a total rated thermal input of at least 10 MW at the site.

benefit.reason: Allowance needs depend on site activities, benchmarks and verified emissions; no amount is calculated.

schemes.publisher: Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, Republic of Korea
schemes.offers_text: Possible compliance exposure: a nationwide emissions trading scheme for industry, with a rising share of auctioned permits.
schemes.who: Entities covered by the K-ETS Act; the ministry page states no threshold, so check the Act and its Enforcement Decree.
numbers_used: The ministry page says nationwide implementation began in 2015 and more than 70% of national GHG emissions are covered.

benefit.reason: Coverage thresholds are not stated on the page and permit needs depend on verified emissions; no amount is calculated.

schemes.official_name: Programa de Prueba del Sistema de Comercio de Emisiones (pilot emissions trading system)
schemes.publisher: Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (SEMARNAT)
schemes.offers_text: Possible compliance exposure: a pilot cap-and-trade programme for energy and industry facilities. The page (22 Oct 2021) gives no later status.
schemes.who: Facilities in the energy and industrial sectors with direct CO2 emissions of at least 100,000 tonnes a year, as stated by SEMARNAT.
numbers_used: Threshold: at least 100,000 tonnes of direct CO2 emissions a year.
Preliminary bases published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación on 1 October 2019.

benefit.reason: The pilot was set up without economic effects for participants and its current phase is not confirmed; no amount is calculated.

schemes.official_name: Low Carbon Transition Facility (LCTF), BNM's Fund for SMEs
schemes.offers_text: Green project financing may be available: a facility for SMEs moving to low carbon and sustainable operations, through participating banks. Available from 3 February 2022 until full utilisation; current availability is not confirmed.
schemes.who: SMEs in all sectors committed to low carbon and sustainable operations, subject to assessment by a participating financial institution.
numbers_used: Financing up to RM10 million per SME, tenure up to 10 years.
Maximum financing rate 5.0% per annum, including guarantee fee; no collateral required.

benefit.reason: The rate offered depends on the lender and the facility may be fully used; no interest difference is calculated without an offered rate and a current loan rate.

schemes.offers_text: Green project financing may be available: a long-term refinance fund through participating banks for importing capital machinery for specified green initiatives.
schemes.who: Manufacturer-exporters in any sector, for capital machinery and accessories for specified green initiatives, through a participating bank.
numbers_used: Launched January 2016 with USD 200 million; EUR 200 million added; BDT 50 billion local-currency fund introduced December 2022 (Bangladesh Bank quarterly review, Oct to Dec 2025).

benefit.reason: The review does not state borrower rates or loan limits; no amount is calculated.

schemes.official_name: Refinance Scheme for Environment Friendly Products/Initiatives
schemes.offers_text: Green project financing may be available: a revolving refinance scheme through banks for listed green products such as solar, biogas, effluent treatment and energy auditor certified machinery.
schemes.who: Borrowers financing a product on the scheme list (70 products in 11 categories), through a participating bank or finance company.
numbers_used: Fund size BDT 10 billion since 2023 (SFD Circular No. 02, 30 August 2023).

benefit.reason: The review does not state borrower rates or loan limits; no amount is calculated.

schemes.official_name: Decision 21/2025/QD-TTg on environmental criteria and confirmation of projects in the green classification list
schemes.publisher: Prime Minister of Vietnam (Government legal document portal)
schemes.offers_text: Green project financing may be available: the decision sets environmental criteria and how investment projects are confirmed as green. It is a classification, not a loan or subsidy.
schemes.who: Investment projects seeking confirmation under the green classification list; check the decision text with a lender.
numbers_used: Issued 4 July 2025, effective 22 August 2025.

benefit.reason: The decision classifies projects; it states no rate, amount or subsidy.

schemes.official_name: Promoting Sustainable and Green Financial Practices (Circular BM 1208)
schemes.offers_text: Green project financing may be discussed with your bank: the circular asks banks to engage significant customers, including oil and gas and industry, on transition plans. It is a requirement on banks, not a loan or subsidy.
schemes.who: Customers of banks licensed in Oman, especially large borrowers in Net Zero 2050 priority sectors (industry, oil and gas, transport, buildings and power).
numbers_used: Circular BM 1208, annex dated 13 October 2024.

benefit.reason: The circular sets requirements for banks; it states no rate, amount or subsidy.
